findings.title: Shared-session match state has an Apple-documented race: group rounds silently drop scores, and the payload is not mergeable
planRefs: 6.1 (XP lands on whichever device opens the final bubble)
findings.planSays: "each turn is a message, and an MSSession makes every turn update one bubble"; a group round accumulates one entry per member in that single bubble (`e: [Entry]`, `sr: [String: Int]`, `closed: Bool`), with no server. P4.1 decodes "selected-message ... on every activation". The only ordering edge case listed is "an old bubble tapped after newer ones".
findings.problem: Every responder builds the next message from the bubble they tapped. In a group chat several members tap the same open-round bubble and play for 60-90 s at the same time, so they all extend the same base state. B sends {A,B}; C sends {A,C}. Each device keeps only whichever session message arrived last, order differs per device, and the other entry disappears from the bubble. Leaderboards then differ per device, the starter's close can be undone by a late submission carrying closed=false, podium XP is awarded from different 'final' bubbles, and two simultaneous Rematch taps create two different round r+1. Even without true simultaneity, a message that arrives while a player is mid-song is lost unless didReceive is handled, because selectedMessage is never refreshed. The schema makes this unrecoverable: `sr` is a counter map and `closed` a plain flag, neither can be merged. This is the normal usage pattern for Round mode, not a corner case. Duels are mostly safe (strict alternation) except simultaneous rematch.
findings.evidence: didReceive(_:conversation:) doc: "There is an inherent race condition when multiple participants send messages using the same session object. You cannot guarantee the order in which the messages are received. To ensure that your app always has the latest data, save your data to a server (for example, using CloudKit) and have your messages just carry an ID for that data." selectedMessage doc: "If this message belongs to a session, then the selected message might not contain the most current data. The selected message is not updated when you receive new messages. Instead, override ... didReceive(_:conversation:)". MSSession doc: "If a later message is sent using the same session, the previous message is removed from the transcript." didReceive is only called "while your extension is active". Forum thread 51728 (2016) reports the same symptom: "chances are you will only end up opening the response that comes in second."
findings.recommendation: Decide this before Phase 1, because it changes Appendix C. Keep no-server, but make state convergent: (1) Entries become a grow-only set keyed by (round, player id); merge = union; same-key conflict resolved deterministically (earliest `t`, then lowest id). `closed` becomes sticky (once seen true, stays true). Replace the `sr` counter map with per-round results (round -> winner id) and derive the series score, so merging is idempotent. (2) Add a per-device MatchStore (one small JSON per match id) holding the merge of every payload this device has decoded or sent. (3) Route didReceive (including mid-song) into MatchStore; MessageComposer always sends merge(MatchStore, selected payload) + own entry, never the selected payload alone. (4) Fork repair: if the tapped bubble lacks the local player's stored entry, show "Your score isn't in this bubble - Re-post", which inserts the merged state without replaying. (5) Award duel/podium XP from MatchStore through an idempotent ledger keyed (match id, round, award kind). (6) Define the concurrent-rematch rule (the round present in the tapped bubble wins; a locally played conflicting round is kept only as a personal best). (7) Add the three-device concurrency test to Phase S2 and to the Phase 4 gate, and add a risk row. (8) Record the fallback in DECISIONS.md if the spike shows too many forks: per-player bubbles for Round mode (no shared leaderboard bubble), or move Round mode to v1.1 on CloudKit as Apple's note suggests.
findings.deviceTest: Three iPhones on three Apple IDs in one iMessage group. A posts a round bubble. B and C both tap it before either sends, both finish, B sends, C sends within about 5 s. Repeat with the order reversed, and once with C offline while B sends. On every device log each decoded payload with the callback that delivered it (willBecomeActive / didSelect / didReceive), arrival time and entry ids, and screenshot the transcript. Current design: expect at least one device whose bubble is missing B or C. Amended design passes when, after at most one Re-post, all three devices show all three entries and award the same podium once.

findings.title: Participant UUIDs are device-scoped and unstable, so they cannot be the player id in the payload
planRefs: 6.4 (Series records per friend, keyed by conversation participant)
findings.planSays: Appendix C: `p` is the "player id: first 8 hex characters of the participant UUID"; `by` is the "starter's player id"; `sr` is "series wins by player id". Section 3 says the scoping will be "verified in the Phase 4 spike" (the spike is Phase S, task S2). 6.4 keys series records "by conversation participant".
findings.problem: The scoping is already documented, not an open question. A UUID that device A writes into the payload is A's private name for that participant; device B has a different UUID for the same person and cannot map `p` to anyone in its own remoteParticipantIdentifiers. On B only one correlation exists: message.senderParticipantIdentifier (B's UUID for whoever sent this version of the bubble), so only the newest entry's author is attributable. As written, `p` works only as a self-asserted id compared against the same device's own local UUID, and that breaks when: (a) the same person opens the bubble on their iPad (different UUID, so the app shows "Your turn" again and accepts a second entry, or a third 'player' in a duel); (b) the user disables and re-enables the app in Messages, or reinstalls (UUID changes mid-match: they can replay, `by` can no longer close the round, `sr` tallies are orphaned); (c) anything tries to key local records by a remote participant from payload data (6.4), which is impossible.
findings.evidence: localParticipantIdentifier doc: "This UUID is scoped to this device. It remains stable as long as the extension is enabled. If the extension is disabled and reenabled, or if the containing app is removed and reinstalled, the UUID for the local participant changes." remoteParticipantIdentifiers doc: "These UUIDs are scoped to this device." senderParticipantIdentifier doc: "The value of this UUID is scoped to the current device. Each device participating in the conversation will have a different UUID for the message's sender." MSConversation exposes nothing else about participants (members: selectedMessage, the two identifier properties, insert/send methods).
findings.recommendation: Change Appendix C now (schema v1 should not ship with this): replace `p` with an app-generated random player id (for example 6-8 random bytes, base64url) created on first launch and stored in profile.json; use it for `by` and for the series data. "Me" = the entry whose id equals my stored id. Key 6.4 series records by the opponent's payload id, not by a participant UUID. Use participant UUIDs only locally and only for two things: (1) `selectedMessage.senderParticipantIdentifier == conversation.localParticipantIdentifier` as the 'did I send the latest version' check; (2) a device-local key for the conversation (hash of the sorted local+remote UUIDs) to bind pending runs to a chat. State the multi-device limit explicitly in 5.2 (identity and progress are per device in v1; a third id in a duel is shown read-only) or add iCloud key-value sync later. Fix section 3: the scoping is documented; S2 only needs to confirm cross-conversation stability and same-Apple-ID behaviour.
findings.deviceTest: Two iPhones on different Apple IDs plus an iPad signed in to iPhone A's Apple ID. Send one session message from A in a 1:1 chat and in a group chat with the same people. On every device log localParticipantIdentifier, remoteParticipantIdentifiers and selectedMessage.senderParticipantIdentifier. Then switch the app off and on in Messages' iMessage-apps list on A and log again. Record: A's local UUID vs the UUID B reports for A (expected different); whether a device's local UUID is the same in both conversations; whether on A's iPad the sender UUID equals the iPad's local UUID; whether the UUIDs change after off/on.

findings.title: Since iOS 17 Messages' resize pan gesture competes with manual touch handling; the plan's SpriteKit touch input is the affected pattern and nothing tests it
findings.planSays: Minimum iOS is 17.0. Input is "multitouch columns, hardware timestamps fed into the game session" in a SpriteKit view; "Touch zones are the bottom 35% of the screen"; holds are touch-and-keep-holding. The only collapse handling is "collapsing mid-song pauses". Phase S and the risk table do not mention gesture conflicts.
findings.problem: On every OS the app supports, the expanded sheet can be dragged down with a vertical pan anywhere in it. Touches delivered through touchesBegan/Moved/Ended (how SKScene/SKView input works) lose to that pan: a thumb that drifts vertically during a hold or a fast tap gets cancelled and the sheet starts to collapse, which pauses the song. A shipping SpriteKit iMessage game reported exactly this on iOS 17, and a later report says even gesture recognizers were overridden. Separately, the bottom 35% touch zone sits on the home-indicator edge: a full app can defer system edge gestures, but an extension's view controller is not the window's root, so that preference is probably ignored (unverified). If this cannot be tamed the core game is unplayable inside Messages, so it belongs in the first spike, not Phase 3.
findings.evidence: Messages framework overview: "In iOS 17, Messages allows you to interactively resize iMessage apps with a vertical pan gesture. Messages handles any conflicts between resize gestures and your custom gestures. If your app uses manual touch handling such as touchesBegan(_:with:), touchesMoved(_:with:), and touchesEnded(_:with:), you can do either of the following: Change your manual touch handling code to use a gesture recognizer instead. Use your UIView to override gestureRecognizerShouldBegin(_:) and return NO when your iMessage app doesn't own the gesture." The same note is on UIView.gestureRecognizerShouldBegin(_:). Forum thread 731127 (Jun 2023): "touches are not being captured inside SpriteKit. Instead, vertical touches are interpreted as attempts to drag the sheet from expanded down to compact mode ... This breaks the app utterly." Apple Frameworks Engineer reply: "If you're using manual touch handling methods, you need to implement UIView.gestureRecognizerShouldBegin to prevent any UIPanGestureRecognizer from beginning." Dec 2023 follow-up in the same thread: "our UIGestureRecognizers are getting overridden by the iMessage Extension container's pan gestures" (unanswered).
findings.recommendation: (1) Specify P3.3 differently: input comes from a dedicated UIKit view layered over the highway, not from SKScene touch methods or SwiftUI gestures. That view owns a custom UIGestureRecognizer subclass that records UITouch.timestamp for began/ended/cancelled, and overrides gestureRecognizerShouldBegin(_:) to return false for recognizers it does not own while a song is playing. (2) Treat touchesCancelled as a hold release, never as a miss. (3) Keep the touch columns above the bottom safe-area inset plus a margin, and keep the top strip of the sheet free of game input so the player can still collapse deliberately. (4) Add spike task S5 with a pass/fail gate before Phase 3 and a row in the section 13 risk table. (5) If the spike fails on some OS version, the fallback is a non-drag design decision to record (for example taps only, no holds) before charts are authored.
findings.deviceTest: iPhones on iOS 17, 18, 26 and 27, extension expanded, spike highway running. Perform 200 two-thumb taps and 20 holds per column with deliberate 30-60 pt vertical drift, then 20 quick swipes that start inside the touch zone and move up from the home indicator and down toward the bottom edge. Log every touchesCancelled, every willTransition(to:) and willResignActive, and (now - UITouch.timestamp) per touch. Pass: zero cancels and zero unintended presentation changes from in-zone touches. Run once with SKScene touch methods (expected to fail) and once with the recognizer + gestureRecognizerShouldBegin design. Also record whether preferredScreenEdgesDeferringSystemGestures = .bottom changes the home-indicator behaviour.

findings.title: Conversations that are not pure iMessage (SMS, RCS, any group with an Android member) are not handled at all
planRefs: 3 (row: Recipients may not have the app yet)
5.5 (URL doubles as the web fallback for people without the app)
findings.planSays: "every run ends in a bubble that reads well even for people who don't have the app yet"; "The bubble image and caption explain the challenge; the message URL falls back to a web page". The only non-happy recipient case listed in P4.5 is "recipient without the app".
findings.problem: Three different audiences are folded into 'recipient without the app'. (a) iPhone on iMessage without the app: sees the template bubble and a store prompt; the web URL is not what opens. (b) Mac: clicking loads the URL in a browser (the only documented use of the web fallback). (c) SMS/RCS conversations: Apple says only that the template layout 'provides support' for SMS devices; interactive message data cannot travel over SMS/MMS/RCS, so nobody in such a chat, including other iPhone users in a mixed group, can tap to play. The extension has no API to tell which kind of conversation it is in, so the app will happily let a player finish a run and post a challenge that no one can answer, and a 400-4,000 character payload URL may land in the chat as text. Mixed iPhone/Android groups are common, and Round mode targets group chats. There is no spike task, no UX and no test for this.
findings.evidence: MSMessageLiveLayout doc: "The template layout automatically provides support for devices that do not support iMessage apps (macOS, iOS 9 and earlier, and SMS devices)." MSMessage.url doc: "If the message is selected on macOS, the system loads the URL in a web browser." HIG, iMessage apps: "Not supported in macOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS." MSConversation has no transport or capability property (only selectedMessage, participant identifiers, insert/send). Forum thread 62331 (2016): "On non iOS 10 devices and macOS I see an ugly http URL alongside the iMessage image." I found no primary source describing exactly what an SMS/RCS recipient receives, so that part is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add to S2 an explicit non-iMessage test (below) and write the outcome into 5.3/5.4 before Phase 4. Then: (1) split the 'recipient without the app' row into the three audiences above with the expected behaviour for each; (2) if a non-iMessage chat produces a degraded message, show a one-line notice on the send screen ("Friends need iMessage to play back") whenever the spike identifies a usable signal (for example an insert/send error), and otherwise make the score-card image self-explanatory without interactivity; (3) make the fallback web page explain 'this needs iMessage on iPhone' rather than assuming the reader can install the app; (4) note in section 3 that the web fallback is primarily for Mac; (5) add a risk row.
findings.deviceTest: From an iPhone with the spike build: (a) a 1:1 chat with an Android phone (RCS and, with RCS off, SMS) or an iPhone with iMessage switched off; (b) a group containing that phone plus a second iPhone that has the app. In each, open the extension, insert and send a session message with a ~400-character URL and one with a ~3,500-character URL, then send a second message on the same session. Record: whether the app is offered in the + drawer; any error from insert/send; exactly what each recipient sees (image, captions, raw URL text, tappable or not); whether the second iPhone's bubble is interactive; whether the second message replaces the first. Also view one normal iMessage bubble on a Mac and an Apple Watch and note what is shown and what a click opens.

findings.title: Selection is sticky and didSelect fires only for a different message; the 5.4 routing table and the iPad mitigation do not cover this
planRefs: 3 (row: Bubble-tap callbacks can differ between iPhone and iPad)
findings.planSays: 5.4 routes "No bubble selected (opened from the app drawer)" to Home and every other row from the selected bubble's state. The iPad mitigation is "Read the selected message on every activation, not only in the tap callback". Phase 4 is done only when the flows work "on iPhone and iPad".
findings.problem: (1) Once a bubble has been tapped, conversation.selectedMessage stays set for the life of the extension and there is no API to clear it. Re-tapping the same bubble produces no willSelect/didSelect, and collapsing does not deselect. So 'no bubble selected' is not a reliable signal for 'opened from the drawer': after viewing any match, expanding again or coming back from Home re-routes into the stale match, and a re-tap of the current bubble cannot be told apart from pressing the expand control. The table has no rule for this. (2) The plan's iPad mitigation is what a 2026 reporter already tried: on iPad (iOS 18 and 26), after taking a turn and sending, tapping the opponent's new bubble often does not open the extension at all, and reading selectedMessage in willBecomeActive/didBecomeActive/didReceive did not help. If that reproduces, the Phase 4 iPad gate cannot be met by code changes.
findings.evidence: Apple staff, forum thread 53167: "If you tap on a single message I would only expect to get the will/didSelect if you select a different message. This is similar to how a table view works ... The selected message and the presentation mode are orthogonal." Same thread, developers: no programmatic deselect; "we have no way to detect that tap versus a tap on the expand [control]". Forum thread 816190 (Feb 2026, iPad Pro M4 and iPad Air, iOS 18 and 26): "When the opponent sends their response and the player taps on the new message bubble, the extension often does not open. The didSelect(_:conversation:) method is not called ... This works perfectly on iPhone"; attempted fixes included checking conversation.selectedMessage in willBecomeActive, didBecomeActive and didReceive; no resolution, Apple DTS asked for a test project. presentationStyle doc: selecting a message launches the extension expanded; the drawer launches it compact.
findings.recommendation: Specify the router in P4.1 as a pure function re-evaluated on willBecomeActive, didBecomeActive, didSelect, didReceive and didTransition(to:), with inputs (presentationStyle, key of selectedMessage, isPending, last-handled message key, a 'user left this match' flag). Add to 5.4: every match screen has an explicit Home action that sets the flag for that message key; the flag clears only when a different message is selected; expanding with a flagged selection goes Home. Add the reproduction below to S2. Decide from its result whether iPad is a supported target or 'best effort', and change the Phase 4 gate and section 1 wording ("iPad works in the expanded view") accordingly. Test whether calling dismiss() once the send has started (so the next tap is a cold activation) avoids the iPad failure; adopt it only if it does.
findings.deviceTest: iPhone and iPad on the newest and oldest supported OS. (1) Tap a bubble, collapse to compact, tap the same bubble: log which of willBecomeActive / willSelect / didSelect / willTransition fire and the value of selectedMessage. (2) Go Home inside the app, collapse, reopen from the + drawer: log whether selectedMessage is nil or still the old bubble. (3) Ten alternating turns between two devices: tap bubble, play, insert, send, let the extension collapse, other side replies, tap the new bubble. Count taps that fail to open the extension, once with requestPresentationStyle(.compact) after insert and once with dismiss() after didStartSending.

findings.title: An iMessage-only extension cannot open URLs, so the 'App Store link' and any external link cannot work as written
planRefs: 5.4 (Update needed, with an App Store link)
findings.planSays: "Payload from a newer app version or a different chart | Update needed, with an App Store link". The app is iMessage-only with "no Home Screen app".
findings.problem: The only sanctioned way for an extension to open a URL is NSExtensionContext.open, and for iMessage apps it is limited to opening the parent app, and only when that parent is on the Home Screen. This app has no such parent. There is no UIApplication in an extension, so SwiftUI Link/openURL will not open Safari or the App Store either. The same limit hits the privacy policy link that Review requires inside the app, song licence/credit links, and any support link.
findings.evidence: NSExtensionContext.open(_:completionHandler:) doc: "In iOS, the Today and iMessage app extension points support this method. An iMessage app extension can use this method only to open its parent app, and only if the parent app is shown on the iOS home screen." Apple staff, forum thread 54410: "The expected behavior is that the iMessage extension can only open URLs in their parent apps." App Extension Programming Guide: an extension cannot "Access a sharedApplication object". Review Guideline 5.1.1(i): "All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in the App Store Connect metadata field and within the app in an easily accessible manner." SKStoreProductViewController doc: it "doesn't support subclassing or embedding" and throws SKUnsupportedPresentationException if embedded (the 2016 forum workaround embedded it).
findings.recommendation: Change 5.4 to: "Update needed: plain instructions ('Update Riff in the App Store') plus, if the spike confirms it works, a modally presented SKStoreProductViewController". Add a rule to 12.2: no feature may depend on opening an external URL; privacy policy, licences and credits are rendered as in-app text (with the web address shown as selectable text). Add the in-app privacy policy screen to P7.2 and the hosted policy URL to P8.2.
findings.deviceTest: In the spike build, from the expanded extension: (1) call extensionContext.open with an https URL and with an App Store URL and log the Bool; (2) load and modally present SKStoreProductViewController for any live app id and record whether the page appears, whether anything is clipped, and whether dismissal returns cleanly to the extension. Run on the oldest and newest supported iOS.

findings.title: 'Portrait only' cannot be enforced by a Messages extension
findings.planSays: "notes travel toward a strike line about 18% above the bottom edge. Portrait only."
findings.problem: Orientation belongs to the host app. Messages rotates on iPhone when rotation lock is off and in every orientation on iPad (plus Split View / Stage Manager widths), and the extension's view is simply resized. Declaring portrait in Info.plist or overriding supportedInterfaceOrientations has no effect. The plan's 'layout from available size' covers widths but there is no rule for a short, wide view in the middle of a song.
findings.evidence: UIViewController.supportedInterfaceOrientations doc: "the system calls this method on the root view controller or the topmost modal view controller that fills the window" (an extension's controller is neither). Forum thread 53981: a developer set UISupportedInterfaceOrientations to portrait and overrode supportedInterfaceOrientations, "But I am still able to rotate the device and see my layout in landscape"; the accepted reply relays Apple Support: extensions "must follow the constraints and behaviors of iMessage". Other threads report UIDevice orientation as unknown inside Messages extensions.
findings.recommendation: Replace "Portrait only" in 4.1 with: "Designed for a tall view. If the game view becomes wider than tall, or shorter than a stated minimum height, the song pauses and an overlay asks the player to rotate back; menus stay usable (scrolling) at any size." Detect it from the view's bounds in layout, not from UIDevice. Add the pause trigger to 4.7 and a rotation case to the P3.1 expanded-view guard and to the iPad test list.
findings.deviceTest: Rotation lock off: rotate an iPhone to landscape while the expanded extension shows the spike highway; log view bounds and safe-area insets before and after, with and without a supportedInterfaceOrientations override. On iPad repeat in both orientations, in Split View at each width, and in a Stage Manager window.

findings.title: 'Submitted' is undefined between insert and Send: the draft can be deleted or never sent, and the run is lost
planRefs: 5.3 (inserts the message into the compose field and the player taps Send)
findings.planSays: "The app inserts the message into the compose field and the player taps Send. Nothing sends automatically." "One submitted score per player per round; restarts before submitting are fine."
findings.problem: Insert only stages a draft. The plan does not say (a) that the expanded view must give way so the player can reach the Send button, (b) what state the app is in while the draft is staged, (c) what happens if the player deletes the draft, taps the staged draft bubble, inserts something else (which replaces it), or leaves. Because 'have I submitted' is read from the tapped bubble's payload, a player whose draft was deleted is sent back to 'Your turn' and has to replay; a good run is gone. didStartSending does not confirm delivery, and insert's completion handler runs on a background queue.
findings.evidence: insert(_:completionHandler:) doc: "This method does not send the message ... The message is not sent until the user taps Send. Subsequent calls to this method replace any existing message in the input field" and "the system calls the completion block on a background queue." isPending doc: true after insert, false once didStartSending is called; lets you tell "whether the conversation's selectedMessage property refers to a message in the transcript (false) or to a message in the Messages app's input field (true)". didStartSending doc: "It does not guarantee that the message will be successfully sent or delivered." didCancelSending doc: called when "the user subsequently deletes the message object." dismiss() doc: "marks the extension as eligible for termination". send(_:completionHandler:) exists (iOS 11+) and may be called "only in response to a user action".
findings.recommendation: Add a small state machine to 5.3 / P4.2: played -> staged -> sending -> confirmed. Persist the finished run (RunSummary + match id + round) synchronously when the song ends. After insert succeeds (hop to the main actor), call requestPresentationStyle(.compact) rather than dismiss() so the callbacks keep arriving, and show "Tap Send to post your score". On didCancelSending, or on any later activation where the tapped bubble lacks the stored entry, offer "Send your score" again without replaying. Treat a selectedMessage with isPending == true as 'not sent yet', never as Waiting. Mark confirmed only when the entry is seen in a non-pending message. Record in DECISIONS.md whether to keep insert or use send(_:) behind an explicit in-app 'Send score' button (fewer states, one less tap).
findings.deviceTest: Log isPending, didStartSending and didCancelSending in four flows: insert then requestPresentationStyle(.compact) then Send; insert, compact, delete the draft from the field; insert then dismiss() then Send; insert, then tap the staged draft bubble. Note in each whether the compose field and Send button are reachable without extra taps, and which callbacks arrive.

findings.title: Pause/resume assumes the extension survives; pause triggers, termination and conversation switches are unspecified
findings.planSays: "Collapsing the view, a call, Siri or leaving Messages pauses at once. Resume shows a 3-beat countdown and restarts audio in sync." "Writes are atomic".
findings.problem: (1) An extension has no UIApplication lifecycle notifications; the plan names the events but not the signals that carry them. (2) Messages may terminate the extension shortly after it resigns active, and warns that asynchronous work may not finish, so a 'paused' run can simply be gone and a result not yet written is lost. (3) MSConversation has no identifier. If the player switches to another chat while a run is paused or a result is pending, nothing ties that run to the original conversation, and the result could be inserted into the wrong chat with another chat's session.
findings.evidence: willResignActive(with:) doc: "Avoid doing any time-consuming tasks ... Also, avoid making asynchronous calls, because the extension might terminate before the asynchronous tasks have completed." Foundation: NSExtensionHostWillResignActive ("Posted when the extension's host app moves from the active to the inactive state") and NSExtensionHostDidEnterBackground ("Extensions receive only a short amount of time to perform any background work"). MSConversation's members are selectedMessage, the participant identifiers and insert/send only.
findings.recommendation: In 4.7 list the pause signals: willTransition(to: .compact), willResignActive(with:), NSExtensionHostWillResignActive, NSExtensionHostDidEnterBackground, AVAudioSession interruption, and the size change from MSG-7. State that a run interrupted by termination is discarded (no partial scores) and that a completed run is written synchronously at song end, before the results screen. Give ConversationContext a device-local conversation key (hash of the sorted local and remote participant UUIDs); bind paused and pending runs to (conversation key, match id, round) and drop or park them when willBecomeActive arrives with a different key.
findings.deviceTest: With a song paused in the spike build: switch to another conversation and back; send Messages to the background for 10 s and for 5 min; lock the screen; take a phone call; invoke Siri. For each, log willResignActive/didResignActive, the two NSExtensionHost notifications, the audio interruption notification, the process id and the view controller's object id on return, and whether in-memory state survived.

findings.title: Phase S depends on TestFlight, but every TestFlight prerequisite is scheduled in Phase 8
planRefs: 12 (two iPhones on two Apple IDs by Phase S)
13 (Recruit a test partner ... in the first week)
findings.planSays: "Recruit one test partner with their own Apple ID and iPhone early, via TestFlight" for Phase S, while icons are P8.1, the privacy manifest P8.2 and TestFlight P8.3. P8.1 says "Messages app icons (4:3 sizes)".
findings.problem: A build cannot be uploaded for TestFlight without the pieces the plan leaves to the last phase: the App Store Connect record, the complete iMessage icon set (not only the wide sizes), a privacy manifest covering required-reason APIs, and the export-compliance answer. External testers also need a first Beta App Review. The privacy manifest must sit in the extension bundle, since the wrapper has no code, and the timing code will likely touch a required-reason category.
findings.evidence: Required-reason API article: "Starting May 1, 2024, apps that don't describe their use of required reason API in their privacy manifest file aren't accepted by App Store Connect" and "For each executable or dynamic library in an app that uses a required reason API, the bundle that includes the executable or dynamic library needs to include a privacy manifest file". The System Boot Time category lists systemUptime and mach_absolute_time(); reason 35F9.1 covers measuring elapsed time between in-app events; File Timestamp reason C617.1 covers files in the app or App Group container; User Defaults reasons are CA92.1 (app only) and 1C8F.1 (App Group). HIG icon table for iMessage apps: Messages sizes 148x110, 143x100, 120x90, 180x135, 64x48, 96x72, 54x40, 81x60, plus Settings 58x58 and 87x87 and App Store 1024x1024. Developer forum reports of upload rejections for a missing iMessage App Icon (ITMS-90649, ITMS-90644, 1024x768 large icon) were seen only as search summaries.
findings.recommendation: Move into P0.2/P0.3: App Store Connect app record and bundle ids; a placeholder 'iMessage App Icon' set with every slot filled (wide Messages sizes, the 1024x768 Messages store icon, the square Settings sizes and 1024x1024); PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in the RiffMessages target with only the categories the code really uses (expected: SystemBootTime 35F9.1 if mach_absolute_time or systemUptime is called directly; FileTimestamp C617.1 if file dates are read; a UserDefaults reason only if UserDefaults is used); the export-compliance key after confirming HMAC-only use is exempt. Add a P0 gate: 'an archive uploads to App Store Connect with no errors'. Keep P8 for final art, the privacy label, age rating, the hosted privacy policy and review notes. Alternatively state that Phase S uses a second device with a second Apple ID installed straight from Xcode, and TestFlight starts in Phase 4.

findings.title: Payload in the query string of an https URL sends match data to the web server, which undercuts 'no network' and 'Data Not Collected'
planRefs: 7.5 (No network, analytics or accounts in v1)
findings.planSays: `https://<domain>/m?p=<payload>` "on a domain we control. That URL doubles as the web fallback"; "any https placeholder for TestFlight"; privacy label "Data Not Collected".
findings.problem: Whenever the URL is opened outside the app (documented for Mac; possibly also wherever it degrades to a plain link), the browser sends the whole payload (nicknames, scores, player ids, timestamps) to that server together with the visitor's IP address. With default access logs the developer then holds that data, which is hard to square with a 'Data Not Collected' label. A placeholder domain owned by someone else would leak it to a third party. Separately, if the decoder checks the host, changing the domain between TestFlight and release breaks every old bubble. A 2016 report says Mac showed the raw URL next to the image, which would be thousands of base64 characters.
findings.evidence: MSMessage.url doc: "If the message is selected on macOS, the system loads the URL in a web browser. The URL should point to a web service that returns a meaningful result based on the encoded data." Apple, App privacy details: "'Collect' refers to transmitting data off the device in a way that allows you and/or your third-party partners to access it for a period longer than what is necessary to service the transmitted request in real time"; "Your app includes game saves, multiplayer matching, or gameplay logic. Declare Gameplay Content on your label"; User ID includes "screen name, handle". Review Guideline 2.1(a): submissions need "fully functional URLs"; "empty websites ... should be scrubbed". Forum thread 62331 for the raw-URL report and Apple staff's suggestion of a data: URL to hide it.
findings.recommendation: In 5.5 and Appendix C: (1) carry the payload in the URL fragment (`https://<domain>/m#p=<payload>`), which browsers never send to the server, and let a static page decode it client-side; verify in S2 that the fragment survives the round trip, and if it does not, keep the query form but host the page statically with access logging off and say so in the privacy policy. (2) The decoder reads the payload item and ignores scheme, host and path, so the domain can change. (3) Never use a domain you do not control, even in TestFlight. (4) The 4 KB cap is defined on the full URL string length and stays under the documented 5,000 characters. (5) The fallback page must be live with real content before submission. (6) Note the Mac raw-URL question as a spike check.
findings.deviceTest: Send a session message whose URL is https://<test-domain>/m#p=<payload>. On the receiving iPhone log message.url.absoluteString and compare byte for byte. On a Mac running current macOS, note what the bubble shows (is the raw URL visible?) and click it; check the server log for what was requested. Repeat with the ?p= form.

findings.title: Bubble spec gaps: no summaryText or accessibilityLabel, an undocumented name placeholder, and a per-viewer element that a sender-rendered image cannot show
findings.planSays: "captions use Messages' participant-name placeholder (verify on device)"; captions such as "Sam scored 412,300"; the round bubble shows "top 3 plus your own place"; VoiceOver work is scoped to "every menu".
findings.problem: (1) summaryText is never mentioned. Each superseded turn is replaced in the transcript by that text, or by a system default if nil, so the visible history of a match is whatever Messages chooses. (2) accessibilityLabel is not set, so VoiceOver has nothing meaningful to read for a score-card image. (3) The '$' + UUID name substitution is not in Apple's current documentation; it rests on a WWDC 2016 session that is no longer published and on developer reports, some of which show a phone number or email when the participant is not in the viewer's Contacts. It also cannot appear in the rendered image, so the caption would say a contact name while the card says a nickname. (4) The image is rendered once by the sender and is identical for everyone, so 'your own place' can only be the sender's place. (5) Two layout facts the card design must respect are missing: the image is cropped 6 points left and right with rounded corners, and a received message has no layout, so nothing can be read back from captions or image.
findings.evidence: summaryText doc: "Set the summary text when you create a message that is associated with a session. When a subsequent message is sent using the same session, the Messages app uses this text to create a summary in the transcript. If the summary text is nil, the system provides a default description". accessibilityLabel doc: "VoiceOver reads this property when describing the message." The caption, trailingCaption and localParticipantIdentifier pages contain no mention of name substitution. Forum thread 52130 cites WWDC16 session 224 for the '$uuid' trick and shows an unreplaced "$E0712CEB-... won!" on one beta; the WWDC16 224 video page now returns no video. A Stack Overflow title found by search reads "iMessage identifiers converted to phone number instead of name" (page not reachable from here). image doc: "The system crops the left and right edges of the image by 6 points, and rounds the image's corners." Apple staff, forum thread 53174: "Received messages won't have a layout object filled in ... Information that needs to be conveyed in the message needs to be encoded in the URL".
findings.recommendation: In 5.3: set summaryText on every message (for example "Sam scored 412,300 on Neon Nights") and accessibilityLabel (a full sentence with scores and standing); use the payload nickname everywhere in captions and summary, and drop the placeholder unless S2 shows it renders a real name for contacts and you accept a phone number for non-contacts; change 5.1 to "top 3 plus the sender's place" (the viewer's own place is shown after tapping); give the score card a safe margin of at least 12 pt and no essential content at the corners; note that all state is read from the URL only. Add VoiceOver for the bubble to P7.3.
findings.deviceTest: Send messages whose caption and summaryText contain "$" + localParticipantIdentifier.uuidString. Record the rendered text on: the sender's device; a receiver who has the sender in Contacts; a receiver who does not; a third member of a group. Then send a second message on the session and record what the summary line for the first looks like with summaryText set and with it nil. Turn on VoiceOver and note what is read for the bubble with and without accessibilityLabel.

findings.title: A group round 'completes when every member has submitted', but the member count includes people who cannot or will not play
planRefs: 6.1 (podium XP lands when the round completes)
findings.planSays: "A group round completes when every member has submitted or the starter closes it." Podium XP lands "when the round completes".
findings.problem: The only member count available is remoteParticipantIdentifiers.count + 1 on the viewing device. It counts members without the app, members who ignore the challenge, and it changes when people join or leave. In practice 'everyone submitted' will almost never be reached, so standings stay provisional and podium XP is never paid unless the starter remembers to close, and only the starter's original device can close (see MSG-2).
findings.evidence: MSConversation offers only remoteParticipantIdentifiers ("An array of UUIDs representing the remote participants in this conversation"); there is no information about who has the app, and the UUIDs change if the extension is disabled and re-enabled. The rest is reasoning from the plan's own rules.
findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic expiry to 5.2: a round is final when closed, when every member counted at start has submitted, or 24 hours after the starter's timestamp carried in the payload, whichever comes first (the duration lives in GameConfig). Finality is computed locally from the payload so all devices agree without a new message; a submission arriving after expiry is shown as late and does not change the podium. Let any participant, not only the starter, close a round after a shorter grace period. Store the member count at start in the payload so 'N of M played' is stable.

findings.title: Compact view cannot show a keyboard and should not scroll horizontally; nickname entry and the song picker need a rule
planRefs: 3 (row: Gameplay needs the expanded view ... Menus work in compact)
findings.planSays: "Menus work in compact; Play requests expanded"; "Players set a nickname".
findings.problem: The compact view replaces the keyboard, so the nickname field cannot be edited there, and Apple's guidance excludes horizontally scrolling content in compact, which rules out a carousel-style song picker in that size.
findings.evidence: MSMessagesAppPresentationStyle.compact doc: "Because the keyboard is not available, adding text fields or text views to your compact layout is not recommended. If you have a control that requires input from the keyboard (for example, a text field), you must call requestPresentationStyle(_:) to expand the extension as soon as the user selects that control ... Additionally, do not include horizontally scrolling elements in a compact layout." HIG: "In general, let people edit text only in the expanded view."
findings.recommendation: Add to the UI spec: compact screens are vertical lists with no text input; focusing the nickname field (first run and Profile) requests expanded first; the song picker in compact is a vertical list.

findings.title: The wrapper app has no code, so 'App Group shared by the wrapper app and the extension' describes nothing in v1
planRefs: 12 (paid membership for App Groups and TestFlight)
findings.planSays: "An App Group container is shared by the wrapper app and the extension." "a paid Apple Developer Program membership (for App Groups and TestFlight)".
findings.problem: An iMessage-only wrapper is a stub product with no source files and never launches, so it cannot read or write the container. The App Group adds an entitlement and provisioning step to two targets for no v1 benefit; its only value is forward compatibility with the 'Later' companion app. If the entitlement is misconfigured the container lookup returns nil, and the plan has no fallback. RiffApp can hold only an Info.plist and an asset catalog.
findings.evidence: XcodeGen ProjectSpec lists `application.messages` and `app-extension.messages`; its source says "simple messages applications without sources should not include a compile sources build phase"; its own test fixture pairs an `application.messages` target with an `app-extension.messages` dependency. XcodeGen ships an icon-name preset ("iMessage App Icon") for the extension product type only. IceCreamBuilder sample: all logic lives in the extension target.
findings.recommendation: Reword 7.5: "Data lives in an App Group container owned by the extension, chosen so a future companion app can read it; if the group container is unavailable, fall back to the extension's Application Support directory." In 7.2 state that RiffApp contains only Info.plist and Assets.xcassets (icon set), and set the icon build setting for that target explicitly in project.yml. Correct section 12: the paid membership is needed for TestFlight and distribution.

confirmedSound: MSSession behaviour matches the plan: a later message on the same session removes the previous bubble and appears at the bottom; an update is made with MSMessage(session: selectedMessage.session). MSSession has no properties, so the payload's own match id is needed and is present.
All state must ride in MSMessage.url: Apple staff confirm a received message has a nil layout, so nothing can be read back from the image or captions. The plan already carries everything in the URL.

URL limits: http, https or data scheme only, at most 5,000 characters (MSMessage.url doc and MSMessageErrorCode.urlExceedsMaxSize). The plan's 4 KB cap is inside that. Recomputed with realistic data (compact JSON, raw deflate, base64url): a 2-entry duel is about 410-540 URL characters; a 32-entry round is about 2,100-3,700 characters depending on nicknames (ASCII about 2,300; random CJK about 3,600; 16 emoji clusters about 3,700). Both of the plan's size claims hold.

An https URL is the right scheme for the fallback: Apple documents that selecting the message on macOS loads the URL in a browser. The HIG states iMessage apps are not supported on macOS, tvOS, visionOS or watchOS.

MSMessageTemplateLayout has exactly the fields the plan needs: image, imageTitle, imageSubtitle, caption, subcaption, trailingCaption, trailingSubcaption. The four caption strings in 5.3 map one to one.
Insert-then-user-taps-Send is the documented default flow, and insert on an existing session updates the bubble only when the user sends.

Presentation: the + drawer launches the extension compact (keyboard area), tapping a bubble launches it expanded, requestPresentationStyle(.expanded) is available, and the user can always collapse. This matches 'menus in compact, Play requests expanded, collapse pauses'.
There is no API for contact names or anything about participants beyond opaque UUIDs, as section 3 says.

Not using MSMessageLiveLayout in v1 is the right call and should be recorded in DECISIONS.md: it still needs a template fallback, it creates one extra view-controller instance per transcript bubble inside a memory-limited extension, selection and receive callbacks are not delivered in transcript style, and developers report live bubbles stuck on 'Loading...' from iOS 17.1 through a July 2026 report on iOS 26 and 27 with no fix.

A standalone iMessage app is a supported App Store product type and can be distributed through TestFlight (Apple's iMessage developer page). XcodeGen supports the wrapper/extension target pair (application.messages plus app-extension.messages).
Review Guideline 4.4 asks extensions to include 'help screens and settings interfaces where possible'; the plan's tutorial, Settings and Profile screens cover this.
The section 3 claim that iOS 27 shipped a first-party Drawing iMessage app is corroborated by web search results (9to5Mac and others); I saw search summaries, not the article itself.
openQuestions: Is localParticipantIdentifier the same in every conversation on one device, and does a message the user sent from their other device arrive with senderParticipantIdentifier equal to this device's localParticipantIdentifier? Apple's docs do not say; the MSG-2 device test settles both.

What exactly do SMS and RCS recipients, a Mac and an Apple Watch show for a template-layout message today, and is the raw URL visible on Mac? No primary source found; the MSG-4 and MSG-11 device tests settle it.
Does a URL fragment survive the MSMessage round trip unchanged? Needed before choosing the fragment form in MSG-11.

What is the real memory limit for a Messages extension on the oldest supported iPhone? Apple publishes none. os_proc_available_memory() is documented to return 0 when 'the calling process isn't an app', so it may not help; the spike may need a debug-only allocation ramp and the limit read from the resulting jetsam report.

Should the turn be posted with send(_:) behind an explicit in-app 'Send score' button instead of insert plus the system Send button? It removes the staged-draft states in MSG-8 but changes the plan's 'nothing sends automatically' wording.

Does the current Xcode simulator's Messages app deliver MSMessage between its two built-in conversations? It was reported broken on the iOS 17 simulator; if it works now, much of Phase 4 can be smoke-tested without a second device.

Guideline 4.4 says extensions 'may not include marketing, advertising, or in-app purchases', while Apple's iMessage page says a standalone iMessage app can add in-app purchase. This needs resolving before the 'Song packs and in-app purchases' roadmap item, and may be a reason to make the companion app the purchase surface.

How does Messages encode layout.image when sending? The plan's 300 KB budget cannot be checked directly from a UIImage; a pixel-size rule (for example 900 x 900 px, opaque) may be the enforceable form.
Is the 32-entry cap tied to the real iMessage group size limit? Not verified here.

Not reachable from this session (network policy): kiwix.lema.org, kaweah.freedombox.rocks, dev.classmethod.jp, openradar.appspot.com. The Stack Overflow reports on the '$' name placeholder (phone number shown instead of a name) and on cross-conversation UUID stability were therefore seen only as search summaries.
